review: owner appearance review of the B5 asteroid prop, first revision
evidence_shown: artifacts/s06_alliance_batch_review/b5-asteroid/asteroid-field-comparison.png (same camera, same field, procedural rock left of each pair and authored prop right)

measured.layout: identical between the two variants - the field's forty placements are unchanged, which is the RNG parity working

reading: The owner prefers the procedural rock the row replaces. In the capture the authored prop reads as soft, oversized, dark clusters - foliage rather than stone - where the legacy rock is crisp and faceted.
causes_identified_in_the_revision: fitted to the legacy rock's worst-case box (+-0.90 x and z, +-0.70 y), so every instance is systematically larger than a typical legacy rock, which is nearer +-0.55

the gridded, noised crust replaced the flat per-face facets that give the legacy rock its read, and carried 3,000 triangles where the legacy is 48-96 - the wrong direction for a prop the field draws forty times
the dark role took 888 of 3,000 triangles and is tinted at 0.62, so the prop sits dark against a bright field
next_revision_plan: fit the prop to the *mean* legacy rock (+-0.58 x and z, +-0.46 y) with the worst case kept as a hard ceiling that is asserted, not reached
return to hard-edged facets: ten small overlapping lumps, each hull subdivided with jittered corner points and flat per-face normals
rebalance the roles so base and trim carry the crust, dark is undersides only, and lift the dark tint
note: Recorded rather than overwritten: this is what the owner was shown and what he said about it. The batch stays pending_owner_appearance_approval, activation stays false, and the row is not registered anywhere.
